featured.title: Sundar Pichai Is Selling $85 Billion of Alphabet to Win the AI Race. Investors Are Divided.
featured.excerpt: The largest equity offering in tech history includes a $10 billion anchor from Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway. Alphabet plans to spend up to $190 billion this year alone — and it ordered three million TPUs from Intel.
featured.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet and Google
featured.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai's most consequential financial gamble reshapes the company tens of thousands of Indian engineers call home — and it may determine whether Google or OpenAI defines the next era of computing.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Dubai and Singapore Have Long Held NRI Money. GIFT City Is Now Making a Serious Bid to Bring It Home.
news.excerpt: With the first Foreign Family Investment Fund approved and Singaporean capital flowing in, India's IFSC at GIFT City is positioning itself as a tax-efficient, India-linked base for diaspora wealth.
news.image_caption: GIFT City near Gandhinagar, India's first International Financial Services Centre
news.nri_angle: GIFT City offers NRIs a tax-efficient, India-linked base for family offices, offshore funds and succession planning — letting the diaspora invest in India's growth without the friction of onshore structures or the geopolitical concentration risk of a single foreign hub.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Britain Is Rewriting Its Immigration Rulebook. For Indians — Its Biggest Migrant Group — One Door Opens as Several Narrow.
news.excerpt: A CETA trade-deal route could let Indian professionals work in the UK for up to a year, even as tougher English tests, a shorter graduate visa and a new student levy raise the cost of British migration.
news.image_caption: Westminster, London; the UK is reshaping visa and settlement rules that affect Indian migrants
news.nri_angle: Indians are the UK's largest migrant group — the biggest source of work visas and among the largest of students — so every shift in British visa, settlement and trade-deal mobility rules directly reshapes the plans of diaspora families studying, working or settling in Britain.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Gulf Crisis Just Reached India's Fields. Sixteen Fertiliser Ships Are Stranded in the Strait of Hormuz.
news.excerpt: With 330,000 tons of urea and 257,000 tons of DAP stuck in contested waters, New Delhi insists the summer sowing season is safe — even as it floats fresh import tenders to plug the gap.
news.image_caption: The bulk carrier Darya Ganga; 16 India-bound ships carrying fertiliser are stranded in the Strait of Hormuz
news.nri_angle: Many NRIs remit money to farming families, own agricultural land, or track India's rural economy — and a fertiliser shortfall at sowing time means higher food inflation, squeezed rural incomes and added pressure on the remittances that cushion millions of households back home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Tells Its Sailors to Stop Going Into the Gulf. Three Were Just Killed There.
news.excerpt: After the MT Settebello strike off Oman, the Directorate General of Shipping has restricted Indian seafarer deployment to conflict zones — a rare operational step as families demand more than protests.
news.image_caption: An oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, where Indian-crewed vessels have come under attack

sources.label: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

news.nri_angle: Indian seafarers make up ~12% of the global maritime workforce; their remittances sustain coastal and northern Indian households, and the Gulf is their most-trafficked and now most-dangerous corridor.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The World's Tech Giants Are Building in Bengaluru, Not Hiring in California. India's GCC Workforce Is Headed for 2.36 Million.
news.excerpt: As US visa policy tightens, multinationals are pouring high-end AI and cybersecurity work into India-based capability centres. N-able's new Bengaluru hub is the latest sign of where global tech is moving.
news.image_caption: The Bengaluru skyline, India's premier technology hub and centre of its GCC boom
news.nri_angle: As H-1B fees rise and green-card backlogs stretch decades, GCCs let Indian engineers build global careers without emigrating — reshaping the calculus NRIs and their families make about returning home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Indian Students Crashed the US Visa Portal on Day One. The Embassy Says Thousands More Slots Are Coming.
news.excerpt: After the June 14 reopening triggered a frantic rush and technical glitches, the US Embassy in India assured applicants that more appointments for July and August will open in the coming weeks.
news.image_caption: The US Embassy in New Delhi, which reopened student visa appointment scheduling this week
news.nri_angle: Indian students are the largest group of international students in the US and the front of the diaspora pipeline — today's F-1 applicants become tomorrow's H-1B workers, green-card holders and citizens.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Germany Just Scrapped the Airport Transit Visa for Indians. Frankfurt and Munich Are Now Open Gateways.
news.excerpt: From June 3, Indian passport holders can connect through German airports to non-Schengen destinations without a Type A transit visa. The fine print still matters.
news.nri_angle: Frankfurt and Munich are among the busiest connecting hubs for Indians flying to North America, so scrapping the transit visa directly eases travel for NRIs, students and visiting families.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: 23 Died in a Delhi B&B That Should Never Have Been Open. The Inspector Who Cleared It Has Been Sacked.
news.excerpt: A six-room licence, 25 rooms in reality, sealed windows and no fire NOC. As Delhi promises a citywide crackdown, critics ask why a cook was arrested before the owners and officials.
news.image_caption: A Delhi Fire Service engine responds to an emergency (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: NRI families visiting India for medical care, weddings and pilgrimages routinely stay in exactly the kind of budget, informally regulated lodgings that turned deadly in Malviya Nagar.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Single Mother Can Now Get Her Child an Indian Passport Without the Father's Signature. The Andhra Court Just Said So.
news.excerpt: Justice Battu Devanand ruled that the prescribed declarations are enough — no paternal consent required. It joins a growing line of high court judgments protecting single parents.
news.image_caption: An Indian passport; courts have repeatedly affirmed a single parent's right to obtain one for a minor

sources.label: Andhra Pradesh High Court (Shaik Shabana v. Union of India)
Telangana High Court / Child Rights Clinic

news.nri_angle: Cross-border custody and long-distance separations are common in NRI families; the ruling gives single parents abroad a clear path to obtain a child's passport without an uncooperative ex's signature.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Canada Has Rewritten Its Immigration Rulebook for 2026. Here Is What It Means for Indians.
news.excerpt: Ottawa slashed generic temporary visas by 43 percent and made occupation-based draws the core of Express Entry. For Indian professionals, a high score is no longer enough — only a precise sector fit gets you in.
news.image_caption: Parliament Hill in Ottawa, where Canada sets the immigration policy reshaping its Express Entry system for 2026
news.nri_angle: Indians are the single largest source of Canadian Express Entry invitations, and the 2026 overhaul reshapes the most reliable migration route out of India away from the American green card backlog.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Pay $750 and Skip the U.S. Visa Line. For Indian Families, the New Fee Cuts Both Ways.
news.excerpt: From July 1, B-1/B-2 applicants can buy an interview within ten business days for $750 on top of the standard fee. It is relief for families facing year-long waits at Indian consulates — and a new equity problem.
news.image_caption: U.S. visa processing now carries a new surcharge for visitors (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: Indian consulates post some of the world's longest visitor-visa waits, so the expedite fee directly affects NRIs trying to bring parents and family to the US for births, weddings, and graduations.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: El Nino Is Here. India's Monsoon Season Faces Its Biggest Threat in a Decade.
news.excerpt: U.S. and Indian forecasters have confirmed El Nino conditions that could slash rainfall, shrink harvests, and push food prices higher as 200 million rain-fed farming households begin sowing.
news.nri_angle: NRI families in agricultural states face higher food prices and increased remittance demand as a weak monsoon threatens rural incomes and consumption.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Kevin Warsh Chairs His First Fed Meeting This Week. Here Is Why NRIs Should Pay Attention.
news.excerpt: The new Federal Reserve chairman presides over a pivotal policy decision on Wednesday as inflation climbs, rate hike odds rise, and every signal from Washington ripples through India's rupee, bond markets, and NRI investment portfolios.
news.image_caption: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivers remarks at his swearing-in ceremony at the White House, May 22, 2026
news.nri_angle: NRIs face direct consequences from the Fed's rate path — from U.S. mortgage rates and investment returns to rupee exchange rates and the attractiveness of India-bound deposit schemes.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The G7 Has Opened in Evian. Iran, Trade, and India's Seat at the Table Are All in Play.
news.excerpt: Modi arrives at the French lakeside summit with a dense agenda: the Iran peace deal, a Trump bilateral on Wednesday, and the visa question that won't go away.
news.image_caption: World leaders at a G7 summit group photo
news.nri_angle: The G7 agenda — Iran oil prices, US-India trade talks, and H-1B visa policy — directly shapes the economic and immigration landscape for millions of NRIs.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Indian Markets Surge as Iran Peace Deal Sends Oil Below $84 and Revives Inflow Hopes.
news.excerpt: Nifty jumps 1.5 per cent, rupee heads for 94.80, and BlackRock says India's $30 billion selloff was overdone. Here is what NRIs should know.
news.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai
news.nri_angle: RBI's new FCNR deposit window and a strengthening rupee make NRI remittances and property investments cheaper — if the oil price drop holds.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Gujarat Has Launched Its Industrial Policy 2026. It Wants Semiconductor Factories, Ultra Mega Projects, and NRI Capital.
news.excerpt: The state expands its priority sectors from nine to sixteen, creates a new category for ₹10,000 crore investments, and puts green manufacturing at the centre of its pitch.
news.image_caption: Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel at an official event
news.nri_angle: Gujarat's semiconductor push, green manufacturing incentives, and GIFT City expansion create new investment channels for the state's 10-million-strong global diaspora.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Will Deploy Air Force Planes to Guard Its Medical Exam. Here Is How the NEET Scandal Unravelled.
news.excerpt: The CBI has arrested 13 people, a headmistress confessed to leaking the physics paper, and 22 lakh students must now retake the test under military-grade security on June 21.
news.image_caption: An Indian Air Force C-17 Globemaster III transport aircraft — the IAF is being tasked with ferrying NEET exam papers to prevent leaks (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: NRI families with children or relatives preparing for medical entrance exams face uncertainty about the integrity of India's examination system.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Factories Are Losing 40 Per Cent of Their Output to Heat. The Economic Cost Could Hit 4.5 Per Cent of GDP.
news.excerpt: In Kanpur, workers are collapsing or returning to their villages. New research shows the growth hit from rising temperatures is nearly double what economists previously believed.
news.image_caption: Workers in an Indian factory — extreme heat is cutting factory output by up to 40 per cent across the country (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: NRIs with investments in Indian manufacturing and families back home face growing risks from a heat crisis that is cutting factory output and threatening the health of vulnerable relatives.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: An Indian Engineer Evacuated His Belfast Flat at 1 A.M. The Mob Did Not Stop to Check Nationalities.
nri-world.excerpt: Days of anti-immigrant violence in Northern Ireland have left South Asian and migrant communities afraid to leave home — and exposed how quickly the diaspora's hard-won success can be erased on the street.
nri-world.image_caption: Police and demonstrators face off on a city street at night during civil unrest
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian professionals who arrived in the UK on skilled-worker visas — filling roles the country actively recruited for — are being swept up in anti-immigrant violence that makes no distinction between an asylum seeker and a chartered engineer, exposing the fragility beneath the diaspora's socio-economic success.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Twenty Years On, a Connecticut Diaspora Group Hands Out Awards to a State Senator It Once Might Have Mentored
nri-world.excerpt: GOPIO-CT's 20th anniversary banquet honored five Indian Americans across politics, business, journalism and engineering — a snapshot of a community that no longer asks permission to belong.
nri-world.image_caption: A spacious banquet hall set with round tables for a formal community event
nri-world.nri_angle: Local diaspora organizations like GOPIO-CT are the connective tissue of immigrant life — translating individual success into collective identity and political clout, and reflecting the anxiety that later generations may let the thread to their heritage go slack.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: He Got Indian Americans Recognized for Federal Contracts in 1981. Congress Just Gave Him a Flag.
nri-world.excerpt: Varinder Bhalla's Special Congressional Award honors four decades of unglamorous, structural work that helped build the legal footing the Indian-American community now takes for granted.
nri-world.image_caption: The United States Capitol dome with the American flag flying against a blue sky
nri-world.nri_angle: Diaspora storytelling celebrates the astronaut, the CEO and the senator while skipping the construction — the earlier generation of organizers who did the procedural, defensive work of arguing the community into America's legal and political frameworks in the first place.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India's Tax Dragnet Tightens Around NRIs. The July 1 Overhaul Will Make Hiding Assets Nearly Impossible.
nri-world.excerpt: A new cross-border information-sharing framework compresses response times to 15 days, assigns dedicated tracking officers, and pulls crypto into the net — all without creating a single new tax.
nri-world.image_caption: Tax documents and a calculator on a desk — the tools of cross-border compliance
nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs across the US, UK, Canada, and the Gulf face tighter scrutiny on foreign bank accounts, RSUs, property, and crypto holdings as India's tax information exchange system accelerates from July 1.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Scrapped Bond Taxes for Foreign Investors. One Billion Dollars Arrived in Three Days.
nri-world.excerpt: The abolition of withholding and capital gains taxes on government securities has triggered a buying spree, compressed yields, and revived India's bid for Bloomberg index inclusion — all while the rupee fights a losing battle against oil prices.
nri-world.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai's Fort district
nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs choosing between FCNR deposits and government bonds now face a genuinely competitive choice — zero-tax bonds at 6.9% versus 7.1% deposit rates with RBI-backed swap incentives.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Thirty-Two Words in Ninety Seconds: Shrey Parikh Wins the 2026 Scripps National Spelling Bee
nri-world.excerpt: The fourteen-year-old from Rancho Cucamonga shattered the spell-off record and extended Indian Americans' two-decade dominance of the country's premier academic competition.
nri-world.image_caption: A contestant at the Scripps National Spelling Bee competition in Washington, D.C.
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-American community has dominated the Spelling Bee for two decades; the victory reflects the diaspora's deep investment in academic competition and a self-reinforcing ecosystem of coaching, regional circuits, and family aspiration.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India's Diaspora Dollars Hit $135 Billion — and They Are the Only Foreign Capital That Never Flinches
nri-world.excerpt: Record remittances in FY25 financed nearly half of India's trade deficit. With $140 billion projected for FY26, the NRI wire transfer has quietly become India's most reliable external lifeline.
nri-world.nri_angle: NRI remittances are the largest single source of hard currency flowing into India, outpacing FDI and FPI; the shift from Gulf blue-collar to US/UK white-collar sources reflects the diaspora's upward mobility; individual NRIs benefit from a weak rupee and competitive deposit rates.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Forty Thousand Restaurants and No Chain: India's Celebrity Chefs Are Finally Coming for the American Market
nri-world.excerpt: Sanjeev Kapoor in Santa Clara, Zorawar Kalra in Bellevue, Rishtedar in Miami — three branded Indian restaurant concepts have opened their first US outposts, betting that the country's $15 billion Indian food market is ready for its Chipotle moment.
nri-world.image_caption: An array of Indian dishes — the US Indian restaurant market is now valued at $15 billion
nri-world.nri_angle: The Indian restaurant market in the US has been built entirely by diaspora independents; the arrival of branded chains from India connects NRI diners to cultural touchstones from home while raising questions about mainstreaming vs. authenticity.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Three Dead, Three Ships Hit: Indian Sailors Are Caught in the Crossfire of America's Iran Blockade
nri-world.excerpt: In the deadliest week for Indian merchant seafarers in years, U.S. Navy strikes on three tankers off Oman killed three crew and forced scores to abandon ship — prompting India to summon the American diplomat twice and demand the attacks stop.
nri-world.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea — Indian-crewed vessels have been repeatedly struck by U.S. forces off the coast of Oman
nri-world.nri_angle: India has 300,000+ seafarers working globally, many from working-class families who depend on maritime income. The Gulf crisis threatens both lives and livelihoods across the diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Silicon Valley's Indian Americans Take Their Case to the FBI as Hindu Temple Attacks Spread Across the Bay Area
nri-world.excerpt: A group of prominent Indian Americans held an extraordinary meeting with federal officials and four police departments this week, demanding faster action on a wave of anti-Hindu vandalism and theft targeting Bay Area temples.
nri-world.image_caption: A Hindu temple in Sunnyvale, California — Bay Area temples have faced a wave of vandalism and hate-motivated attacks
nri-world.nri_angle: The Bay Area's Indian-American community — among the wealthiest and most professionally accomplished in the country — confronts the unsettling reality that its sacred spaces are being targeted, forcing community leaders into unfamiliar territory as security advocates.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Modi and Macron Open Bharat Innovates in Nice. The Real Story Is the 120 Startups Behind Them.
nri-world.excerpt: India's maiden deep-tech showcase brings 120 startups, 500 investors, and 13 sectors to the French Riviera — one day before the G7.
nri-world.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with French President Emmanuel Macron at a bilateral meeting in Mumbai
nri-world.nri_angle: The conclave gives NRI investors and entrepreneurs in Europe a structured way to connect with Indian innovation, while showcasing India's deep-tech ecosystem to global capital for the first time at this scale.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Margin of Seventy People: India Just Overtook England as Australia's Largest Source of Overseas-Born Residents
nri-world.excerpt: For the first time since records began in 1891, a non-British-origin group tops Australia's migration charts. The Indian-born population grew by 522,000 in a decade.
nri-world.image_caption: The Sydney Opera House and harbour — home to one of Australia's largest Indian-born communities
nri-world.nri_angle: Nearly a million Indians now call Australia home, making it the fourth-largest Indian diaspora community in the world. The milestone reshapes the conversation about belonging and identity for Indian Australians.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Wholesale Inflation Just Hit a Six-Month High of 9.68%. Why the RBI Is Not Panicking — and What It Means for NRIs.
markets-finance.excerpt: May wholesale price inflation came in far above forecasts at 9.68 per cent, driven by a 61 per cent surge in petroleum and gas prices from the Middle East energy shock. Yet retail inflation sits below 4 per cent and the rupee is rallying — a divergence diaspora investors and remittance senders need to understand.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian rupee notes and coins, as wholesale inflation climbed to a six-month high in May
markets-finance.nri_angle: The gap between soaring wholesale prices and tame retail inflation, combined with a rallying rupee, directly shapes how far NRI remittances stretch and whether the Reserve Bank moves on rates — decisions that affect every diaspora family sending money home or invested in Indian assets.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Foreigners Dumped ₹62,800 Crore of Indian Stocks This Month. Then the RBI Quietly Reopened the Debt Door.
markets-finance.excerpt: As foreign portfolio investors pulled a record ₹2.87 lakh crore from Indian equities in 2026, New Delhi scrapped taxes on government bonds and subsidised NRI deposit hedging — triggering over $1 billion of foreign bond buying in days and reshaping where diaspora money should look.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai (Wikimedia Commons)
markets-finance.nri_angle: The RBI's package directly targets non-resident Indians — fully subsidising hedging costs on three-to-five-year NRI dollar deposits until September — while the bond-tax overhaul changes the risk-reward calculation for diaspora investors weighing Indian equities against fixed income.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Kevin Warsh Takes the Chair at a Fed Nobody Agrees On. For NRI Investors, This Week Changes Everything.
markets-finance.excerpt: The new Fed chair's first meeting lands as inflation hits a three-year high, Iran peace sends oil tumbling, and the rupee claws back toward 94. The dot plot may already have shifted under him.
markets-finance.image_caption: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivers remarks at his swearing-in ceremony at the White House, May 2026
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors face a pivotal week: the Fed's rate path directly affects dollar deposit yields, rupee remittance math, and the attractiveness of Indian vs US equities.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Inflation Just Hit a New-Series High. For NRIs, the Real Number Is Much Worse.
markets-finance.excerpt: Official CPI rose to 3.93% in May, but food inflation is at 4.78%, fuel prices have been hiked four times, and the RBI just raised its full-year forecast to 5.1%. Every rupee you send home now buys less than it did in January.
markets-finance.image_caption: A government official briefs media on inflation — India's consumer price index has hit a new series high, with NRI purchasing power eroding faster (Wikimedia Commons)
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI remittances are worth less in real terms as India's food and fuel inflation accelerates — the RBI's revised 5.1% forecast for FY27 means the purchasing power of every dollar sent home is eroding faster than at any point since the new CPI series launched.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Doubled Its Gold Tariff. Smugglers Are Making ₹25 Lakh Per Kilo Bar. NRIs Are Caught in the Middle.
markets-finance.excerpt: The 15 per cent import duty was meant to defend the rupee. Instead it has fuelled a grey-market revival that could hit 100 tons this year — while JP Morgan forecasts $6,000 gold by December.
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs buying gold for weddings or investment now face an 18.45 per cent embedded tax in India — reshaping how and where the diaspora acquires gold.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Oil Below $86, Rupee at 95, Markets Up 2%. The Iran Peace Deal Could Reshape Every NRI Financial Calculation.
markets-finance.excerpt: Brent crude plunged to a three-month low. The rupee posted its best single-day gain in weeks. Indian equities had their strongest session in two months. Here is what it means for your money.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, India

markets-finance.title: India's SIP Machine Has Grown Tenfold in a Decade. Equity Mutual Fund Flows Just Hit a One-Year Low. What NRIs Should Read Into Both.
markets-finance.excerpt: Monthly SIP contributions surged from ₹3,189 crore to ₹30,954 crore in ten years even as foreign investors dumped a record $30 billion of Indian stocks in 2026.
markets-finance.image_caption: Stock market trading screens displaying financial data and market movements
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs deciding whether to stay invested in India face a structural shift: domestic SIP-driven capital now provides floor support that makes timing the market from abroad harder, while FCNR deposits offer a complementary low-risk dollar yield.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Foreign Investors Have Fled 43 of India's 50 Biggest Stocks. Domestic Money Is Filling the Void.
markets-finance.excerpt: FII ownership in Indian equities has plunged to a 14-year low of 14.7 per cent, while domestic institutional holdings have surged to a record 18.9 per cent — a structural shift that reshapes risk and opportunity for NRI investors.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai — foreign institutional investors have pulled back from most of India's top 50 stocks
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors face a double bind: the record foreign exit from Indian equities has eroded returns in dollar terms, but the structural shift toward domestic ownership may reduce future volatility and create a more favourable entry point.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India’s IT Stocks Have Lost 27 Per Cent This Year. For NRI Tech Workers, the Pain Is Doubly Personal.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Nifty IT index has shed more than a quarter of its value in 2026 as AI disruption fears collide with macro headwinds. For the millions of Indian-origin professionals who work in the same industry they invest in, the exposure is uniquely concentrated.
markets-finance.image_caption: A stock market trading screen displaying real-time financial data and price movements
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI tech workers often hold ESOPs in Indian IT firms, invest in IT-heavy mutual funds, and work in the very sector AI threatens to disrupt — creating a rare triple concentration of career, portfolio, and identity risk.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: GIFT City Just Got Its First US Company Listing. Here Is What NRIs Need to Know.
markets-finance.excerpt: Banking assets at $111 billion, US stocks now accessible, and the first American IPO on Indian exchanges — India's answer to Dubai and Singapore is crossing a threshold.
markets-finance.image_caption: GIFT One tower in Gujarat — the centrepiece of India's first International Financial Services Centre
markets-finance.nri_angle: GIFT City is positioning itself as a tax-efficient hub specifically for NRI wealth management, cross-border investing, and India-linked portfolios — a direct alternative to routing capital through Dubai or Singapore.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Just Opened Its Stock Market to Every Foreigner on Earth. Here Is What Changed Overnight.
markets-finance.excerpt: A sweeping FEMA amendment notified on June 12 replaces the NRI-only investment framework with one that lets any individual residing outside India buy and sell listed Indian equities — a historic shift in capital account liberalisation.
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs already invested in Indian equities now share the playing field with every foreign individual globally — understanding the new rules, limits, and safeguards is essential to protect existing holdings.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Indian Banks Are Offering NRIs Up to 7% on Dollar Deposits. Here Is How to Get the Best Rate Before September.
markets-finance.excerpt: The RBI's unprecedented forex swap has sparked a rate war among banks. Emkay calculates leveraged returns could reach 22%. The window closes September 30.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs can now earn 6-7% on dollar deposits at Indian banks with zero currency risk before the RBI's concessional swap window closes September 30.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: He Was the Most Feared Hitter in the IPL. In Dambulla, the 15-Year-Old Is Learning How Hard Cricket Can Be.
sports.excerpt: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's 21 off 14 against Sri Lanka A continued a quiet run in the India A tri-series — a sobering interlude before the youngest debutant in Indian cricket history walks out for the senior team in Ireland and England.
sports.image_caption: India A and Rajasthan Royals batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
sports.nri_angle: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's rise from a Bihar farmer's son to the youngest player set to debut for India embodies the sacrifice-and-aspiration story that resonates deeply with NRI families, who will follow his summer tour of Ireland and England as a symbol of what their own children might achieve.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Manpreet Singh Equalled a 412-Cap Record. In Rotterdam, a Late Drag Still Broke Indian Hearts.
sports.excerpt: India twice clawed level against the Olympic champions before Tijmen Reyenga's 40th-minute strike sealed a 2-3 defeat in the FIH Pro League's European leg — a dress rehearsal on the very turf that hosts the World Cup in August.
sports.image_caption: India midfielder Manpreet Singh, who equalled the national record of 412 international caps
sports.nri_angle: Hockey is the sport India once owned, and its fortunes carry deep emotional weight for NRIs; with the FIH World Cup looming in August on the same Dutch turf, India's narrow 2-3 loss to the Olympic champions is a high-stakes dress rehearsal for the diaspora's oldest sporting dream.

sports.title: India Did Not Qualify. On Tuesday, a Punjabi Mother's Son Carries Its Flag at the World Cup Anyway.

technology.nri_angle: Any NRI who still keeps an Indian SIM for banking, family, or UPI knows the relentless spam-call problem; Equal AI is building voice models for exactly the multilingual, code-mixed reality the diaspora lives in.

technology.nri_angle: NRIs who hold or trade crypto on Indian exchanges face a 30% flat tax, 1% TDS, and now algorithmic data-matching that flags undisclosed gains — making record-keeping a compliance necessity, not an afterthought.

technology.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of South Asian immigrants drive for Uber and Lyft in U.S. cities; a law limiting arbitrary 'deactivations' directly affects their job security, while the platforms argue it forces them to keep unsafe drivers.

technology.image_caption: A satellite orbiting Earth, used to illustrate space-based Earth observation
technology.nri_angle: India's push for sovereign space-AI infrastructure opens cross-border investment and engineering opportunities for NRIs in deep tech, while reducing the country's dependence on foreign satellite-data providers.

technology.image_caption: Office workstations in a Silicon Valley technology company
technology.nri_angle: A pink slip means a 60-day grace period to find a new sponsor or leave the country — a deadline that turns every layoff round into an immigration emergency for thousands of Indian engineers on H-1B and L-1 visas.

technology.nri_angle: Indian-American households are heavily concentrated in tech equities and equity compensation — RSUs, ESPPs, and chip-heavy index funds — so a $1.3 trillion swing in AI semiconductors lands directly on diaspora net worth, not just on Wall Street screens.

lifestyle-health.title: The Nightly Drink Was Never Harmless. A Review of 7,200 Studies Just Put a Number on the Risk.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Research published in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs finds the safest amount of alcohol is none — and that the old ‘two drinks a day’ limit carries a 1-in-25 lifetime risk of death. For a diaspora where social drinking is rising fastest among the young and the affluent, the math is worth reading carefully.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Red wine being poured into a glass, the kind of nightly drink a new study says carries more risk than long assumed
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Alcohol consumption is climbing fastest among young, affluent, and urban Indians and second-generation diaspora professionals, even as the community already carries elevated liver-disease and cancer susceptibility — making a clear-eyed read of the new dose-risk math especially relevant to NRI families.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Decade of Brain Scans Shows the MIND Diet Slows Ageing in the Brain. The Indian Plate Is Halfway There.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A Framingham Heart Study analysis published in the Journal of Neurology, Neurosurgery & Psychiatry tracked brain structure over ten years and found that people who stuck closest to the MIND diet had measurably younger-looking brains. Much of what it rewards — leafy greens, beans, whole grains — already lives in the diaspora kitchen.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A fresh salad of leafy greens and vegetables, the dietary foundation the MIND diet links to slower brain ageing
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The MIND diet's brain-protective core — leafy greens, legumes, whole grains, and nuts — overlaps heavily with traditional Indian regional cooking, giving diaspora families a built-in advantage against cognitive decline if they resist the drift toward fried and ultraprocessed convenience food.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Just 90 Minutes of Lifting a Week Cuts Death Risk. For South Asians, There Is No Cheaper Insurance Policy.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A 147,000-person study spanning three decades, published in the British Journal of Sports Medicine, found the clearest survival benefit at 90 to 119 minutes of weekly resistance training — a finding that matters acutely for a community that loses muscle faster and earlier than almost any other.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Resistance training delivers outsized survival benefits, new research finds (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry less skeletal muscle and more visceral fat at any given weight, so the protective payoff from a modest weekly lifting habit is disproportionately large for the diaspora's aging parents and midlife professionals.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Working From Home Made You an Hour Lonelier Every Day. A Half-Million-Person Study Just Proved It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Remote workers in 'remotable' jobs — overwhelmingly in tech — spend an extra hour alone each workday and don't make up for it after hours. For South Asian professionals 10,000 miles from family, the numbers hit differently.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A man working alone from home on his laptop in a quiet indoor setting
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech professionals are disproportionately in 'remotable' jobs, and they already carry the baseline isolation of living thousands of miles from extended family — making the mental health costs of remote work a doubled burden.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: South Asian Women Hit Menopause Four Years Before the American Average. The Wellness Industry Has Barely Noticed.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A major study of South Asian American women finds the mean age at natural menopause is 48 — four years earlier than the US norm of 52. Nearly a third experienced premature or early menopause. Apple just launched a programme for everyone else.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A middle-aged woman working out on a gym machine for a healthy lifestyle
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian American women enter menopause years earlier than the national average, face more severe symptoms, and navigate cultural taboos that discourage open discussion — a triple burden the mainstream wellness industry has yet to address.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Grandmother's Filter Kaapi May Be the Best Diabetes Drug Nobody Prescribed. A Genetic Study Just Showed How.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Unsweetened filter coffee uniquely promotes a gut bacterium that lowers blood sugar — and the mechanism maps perfectly onto the South Indian decoction ritual millions of diaspora families still follow.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A tumbler and davara of South Indian filter coffee, the traditional serving style found in homes and cafes across Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Millions of NRI families from South India still use the stainless-steel filter their parents brought over — and new genetic evidence suggests this exact brewing method has unique diabetes-prevention properties relevant to a community with elevated Type 2 risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Yoga Mats at the Lincoln Memorial, a Guru at Times Square. The Diaspora's Yoga Day Has Grown Up.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The 11th International Day of Yoga arrives themed around healthy ageing — and for NRIs managing parents' health across oceans, the timing could not be sharper.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Yoga practitioners at an International Day of Yoga celebration
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: International Day of Yoga events across US cities offer NRIs practical tools for managing their own and their parents' healthy ageing from abroad.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Ozempic Users Are Exercising Less, Not More. For South Asians, That Is a Dangerous Trade-Off.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study of 753 GLP-1 users found daily steps fell 11 per cent and active minutes dropped 21 per cent after starting treatment. Muscle loss is the hidden cost.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A GLP-1 receptor agonist medication pen
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians are among the fastest-growing users of GLP-1 drugs but face compounding muscle-loss risk due to lower baseline skeletal muscle mass.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Gut Bacteria Decide How Many Calories You Actually Absorb. A New Model Just Proved It.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Arizona State researchers built a mathematical model that tracks food beyond the label. For South Asians losing their traditional diet, the implications are enormous.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Illustration of human gut microbiota — new research shows these bacteria determine how many calories the body actually absorbs (Wikimedia Commons)

lifestyle-health.title: A Heat Wave Is Sweeping the US as the World Cup Kicks Off. South Asians Are Uniquely at Risk.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: More than 200,000 heat deaths in Europe since 2022. A scorching American summer ahead. And a diaspora population that thinks it knows heat but is dangerously wrong about this kind.

CNN Health - US heat wave health guidance, June 2026

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs attending World Cup games and hosting elderly parents from India this summer face unique heat risks that Indian heat tolerance does not prepare them for.

lifestyle-health.title: A $2 Tuberculosis Vaccine Just Normalised Blood Sugar in Type 1 Diabetics. South Asians Should Pay Attention.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: BCG shots reprogrammed malfunctioning white blood cells and slashed insulin use in adults with lifelong Type 1 diabetes — bypassing the pancreas entirely.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An adult with Type 1 diabetes wearing an insulin pump and continuous glucose monitor
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians have the second-highest Type 1 diabetes incidence globally, and BCG is already manufactured at scale by India's Serum Institute — making this both a medical and supply-chain story for the diaspora.

lifestyle-health.title: Losing Belly Fat Saved Brains for a Decade. Losing Weight Did Not. Why South Asians Cannot Ignore This Study.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A 16-year MRI study of 533 adults found that visceral fat — not body weight — drives brain shrinkage. South Asians carry more of it than almost any other group.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: MRI brain imaging used to track long-term effects of visceral fat on cognitive function
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry disproportionately high visceral fat at normal BMI — this study shows that invisible belly fat, not weight, drives brain ageing and dementia risk, making it directly relevant to diaspora health screening.

carousel.title: Dubai and Singapore Have Long Held NRI Money. GIFT City Is Now Making a Serious Bid to Bring It Home.
carousel.excerpt: With the first Foreign Family Investment Fund approved and Singaporean capital flowing in, India's IFSC at GIFT City is positioning itself as a tax-efficient, India-linked base for diaspora wealth.
carousel.image_caption: GIFT City near Gandhinagar, India's first International Financial Services Centre
carousel.nri_angle: GIFT City offers NRIs a tax-efficient, India-linked base for family offices, offshore funds and succession planning — letting the diaspora invest in India's growth without the friction of onshore structures or the geopolitical concentration risk of a single foreign hub.

carousel.title: India's Wholesale Inflation Just Hit a Six-Month High of 9.68%. Why the RBI Is Not Panicking — and What It Means for NRIs.
carousel.excerpt: May wholesale price inflation came in far above forecasts at 9.68 per cent, driven by a 61 per cent surge in petroleum and gas prices from the Middle East energy shock. Yet retail inflation sits below 4 per cent and the rupee is rallying — a divergence diaspora investors and remittance senders need to understand.
carousel.image_caption: Indian rupee notes and coins, as wholesale inflation climbed to a six-month high in May
carousel.nri_angle: The gap between soaring wholesale prices and tame retail inflation, combined with a rallying rupee, directly shapes how far NRI remittances stretch and whether the Reserve Bank moves on rates — decisions that affect every diaspora family sending money home or invested in Indian assets.
